liberty.expression.9.why: Whether mocking religion, even the majority's, should be legal: secular liberals, libertarians, anarchists, socialists and Leninists say yes, while theocratic, integralist, Islamist, Buddhist-nationalist and harmony-state camps keep blasphemy or religious-feelings laws.

notes.JR: Jefferson's Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom (1786) says opinions in matters of religion are outside civil authority: +3.
notes.RE: Voltaire's campaign against the Church ('Écrasez l'infâme') and his defence of the Calas case treat satire of religion as protected reason: +3.
notes.HO: Hoxha's Albania declared itself the world's first atheist state in 1967 and made mockery of religion state policy: +3.
notes.JA: The Jacobin-era de-Christianisation and Cult of Reason mocked the Church openly: +2.
notes.WA: Saudi law punishes insult to Islam with severe penalties up to death on apostasy and blasphemy charges: -3.
notes.AUC: Singapore's Penal Code s.298 and the Sedition Act punish wounding religious feelings in the name of harmony: -2.
notes.CST: Catholic teaching condemns blasphemy and the Church reacted to Charlie Hebdo by urging limits on insulting the faithful: -2.
notes.BN: Buddhist nationalists in Myanmar and Sri Lanka push blasphemy prosecutions against those who insult Buddhism: -3.
